title: Effective descent glues along compatible invariant opens
statement: Let p:X\to Y be a singleton fpqc covering of schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] and let D be a transport descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum] on V\to X. Let (U_i)_{i\in I} be an open covering of V [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each i suppose a descent datum E_i on U_i\to X is given, and the inclusion U_i\to V intertwines its transport with D for every test scheme and pair of maps to X with equal image in Y. If each E_i is effective, then D is effective. No affine or finite morphism hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Descent, Lemma 35.35.13, Tag 0AP4, proof; transport formulation and general singleton fpqc covering

proof.text: If needed, select one covering open for each point of V to obtain a small index type. Choose an effective model W_i over Y and a transport-invariant cartesian projection q_i:U_i -> W_i for each E_i. Transport compatibility of the inclusions identifies each E_i with the restriction of D. Inverse transport supplies reverse invariance. Thus each intersection U_i intersect U_j is invariant under the restricted data.

The projection q_i is a base change of the fpqc cover p. Identify its double pullback with the two transports on U_i, using the effective pullback square. The invariance of U_i intersect U_j says its preimages under the two projections agree. Apply open-subscheme fpqc descent to obtain a unique open W_ij of W_i whose inverse image is U_i intersect U_j.

The identity of U_i intersect U_j intertwines the two restricted data. Under the effective pullback identifications it is a compatible base-change morphism between W_ij and W_ji. Fpqc descent of morphisms supplies a unique transition isomorphism; descend the inverse likewise. Injectivity gives the inverse, identity and triple cocycle laws. The descended preimages of the triple intersections agree by uniqueness of descended opens.

Use Scheme.GlueData to glue the W_i along W_ij and the transition isomorphisms to a scheme W. Their structure morphisms to Y agree on overlaps by fpqc faithfulness, so glue to W -> Y. The projections U_i -> W_i -> W agree on overlaps and glue to q:V -> W. Their cartesian squares identify the open cover U_i of V with the base changes of the covering W_i of W. The local identifications and their inverses glue to an isomorphism V = W times_Y X, so the resulting square is cartesian. For any test-scheme point a of V, restrict its source to the inverse images of the U_i. On each such open transport compatibility and invariance of q_i give invariance of q; morphism extensionality on an open cover gives it globally. Thus W and q witness D.IsEffective. If V is empty, use the empty Y-scheme, whose pullback is empty; transport invariance is unique.

lean.statement: theorem isEffective_of_effective_open_cover {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Y} (hp : Presieve.singleton p ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage Y) {V : Over X} (D : Over.DescentDatum p V) {I : Type v} (U : I → V.left.Opens) (hcover : ∀ x : V.left, ∃ i, x ∈ U i) (E : ∀ i, Over.DescentDatum p (Over.mk ((U i).ι ≫ V.hom))) (hcompat : ∀ (i : I) {T : Scheme.{u}} (f₁ f₂ : T ⟶ X) (h : f₁ ≫ p = f₂ ≫ p) (a : Over.mk f₁ ⟶ Over.mk ((U i).ι ≫ V.hom)), ((E i).transport f₁ f₂ h a).left ≫ (U i).ι = (D.transport f₁ f₂ h (Over.homMk (a.left ≫ (U i).ι) (by simpa only [Over.mk_hom, Category.assoc] using Over.w a))).left) (heffective : ∀ i, (E i).IsEffective) : D.IsEffective
